audit.recode_to: No rule change. Fold kaqc1274 into the kaqc1270 Kaqchikel record (as V44 our earlier reading already ruled 'counted as one language with another entry'); if a separate display row is kept, restore its own deciding quote (Bennett 2016 sec. 6.1, held) in quote/cite/loc and label Berinstein 1979 as language-level corroboration from Patzicía speakers, not as a source on the Southern variety.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: Berinstein 1979 downloaded from eScholarship and read as page scan; all three quoted passages (pp. vi, 47, 52) are verbatim at the stated pages, plus a fourth at p. 3. (2) Identity: Glottolog 5.1 row kaqc1274 = 'Kaqchikel, Southern', bookkeeping=True, family book1242, iso ckf; ISO CR 2008-053 merged ckf into cak because these 'are in fact dialects or dialect groups within a single language'. The web catalog currently shows three Kaqchikel rows (kaqc1270 Cakchiquel StressTyp2 fixed-strict; kaqc1274 Southern and kaqc1275 Northern, an earlier compilation, fixed-dominant). The kaqc1274 row's displayed source (Berinstein) is about Patzicía, Chimaltenango speakers (p.47), outside the retired Southern area, and its original deciding quote (Bennett 2016) is a statement about Kaqchikel as a whole; so nothing in the record is specific to the Southern variety. UCLA Working Papers in Phonetics 47 (UCLA MA thesis), pp. v-vi (abstract), 3, 47-53 — read as scanned PDF downloaded from eScholarship,https://escholarship.org/uc/item/0t0699hc(pages read visually; scan …
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (downloaded) (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.quote: p. 47: "To distinguish these hypotheses the perception experiment was repeated with speakers of Cakchiquel, a related Mayan language, which has fixed final stress and no phonemic length." Also abstract p. vi: "Both K'ekchi and Cakchiquel have fixed final stress but they differ in that while K'ekchi has phonemic vowel length, Cakchiquel does not." And p. 52: "the final syllable (the normal location of stress) will be longer than any other syllable in the word."

sources.note: OKMA municipio-by-municipio dialect survey (phonological variation chapter) — the only work likely to say whether the varieties south of Antigua (retired [ckf]) depart from the pan-Kaqchikel final-stress rule or have extra penult-stress lexemes; our record for 'Southern' rests on Patzicía subjects (Berinstein) and a language-level survey line (Bennett 2016).
